description: One custom-0 instruction, FDOT10.S. It computes up to 10 chained single-precision multiply-accumulate steps of the matrixmul GEMM k-loop (C[i][j] += A[i][k]*B[k][j]) in a single instruction. Each step is rounded exactly like the application's own non-fused code, so results are bit-identical. The workload multiplies 10x10 matrices 30,000 times. One FDOT10.S produces a whole C[i][j], so there are 100 invocations per multiply and 3,000,000 per profiled kernel call. PicoRV32 RV32IM has no FPU, so every float MUL and ADD is a soft-float routine costing hundreds of cycles. Replacing 10 MACs (20 soft-float calls plus index arithmetic and C loads and stores) with one 21-word streaming instruction gives about 0.24 MAC per operand word moved. The kernel is 99.5% of cycles, so the Amdahl ceiling is about 218x.

instructions.name: Float 10-term dot-product-accumulate
instructions.pseudocode:
acc_0 = in[20]
for k in 0..9:                       // fixed trip count 10
    a_k = in[2*k]
    b_k = in[2*k + 1]
    p_k = f32_mul_rne(a_k, b_k)
    acc_{k+1} = f32_add_rne(acc_k, p_k)
t = acc_10
is_nan = ((t & 0x7FFFFFFF) > 0x7F800000) ? 1 : 0
m = 0 - is_nan                       // all-ones if NaN else 0 (mask select)
res = (0x7FC00000 & m) | (t & ~m)
out[0] = res
for w in 1..20: out[w] = 0
rd = res
instructions.semantics: Operand block ABI: rs1 holds the word-aligned address of a 21-word input block in[0..20]. rs2 holds the word-aligned address of a 21-word output block out[0..20]. All words are IEEE-754 binary32 bit patterns. Packing, interleaved so the hardware can stream pairs: for k = 0..9, in[2k] = a_k = A[i][k] and in[2k+1] = b_k = B[k][j]. in[20] = c, the starting accumulator: +0.0 (0x00000000) for a fresh C element, or the previous partial sum when an inner dimension longer than 10 is chained over several invocations. Computation: acc_0 = c, then for k = 0,1,...,9 in that order: p_k = a_k * b_k and acc_{k+1} = acc_k + p_k. Every multiply and every add is a separate IEEE-754 binary32 operation rounded to nearest, ties to even. Nothing is fused and there is no wider intermediate precision. This is exactly the order and rounding of the application's loop `C = C + A*B` over k, so the result is bit-identical to the software. Subnormals are fully supported as inputs and results: no flush-to-zero and no denormals-are-zero. NaN: if acc_10 is any NaN (exponent all ones and fraction nonzero), the result is the canonical quiet NaN 0x7FC00000. Otherwise the result is acc_10's exact bit pattern, including signed zero and infinities. So inf*0 or (+inf)+(-inf) anywhere in the chain yields 0x7FC00000. Rounding mode is fixed at RNE, no fcsr is read or written (the core has no F extension), and all FP exception flags are discarded. Shorter inner dimensions (K < 10): the caller sets the unused pairs to a_k = b_k = +0.0. Each padding step then adds p_k = +0 to the accumulator, which leaves it unchanged unless it is -0, which becomes +0. A chain that starts from c = +0 (clearMatrix) can never hold -0, so padding is exact for the application. Outputs: out[0] = result, and out[1] through out[20] are each written with 0x00000000. The result is also written to rd (pcpi_wr=1, pcpi_rd=result), so the caller stores it straight to C[i][j]. If rd = x0 the register write is dropped as usual. Timing: latency is fixed and independent of operand values. The hardware streams the 20 interleaved words a pair at a time (2 words of operand state, not a 21-word buffer). For each pair it does a 24x24 unsigned mantissa multiply (the core's fast_mul is not reachable from PCPI, and this is a float significand multiplier, not a duplicate 32x32 integer MUL), then a fixed-width align/add/normalize/round with no early exit on zero, subnormal, infinity or NaN. Every pair takes the same number of cycles. It then writes the 21 output words. pcpi_wait is raised the cycle after pcpi_valid (within the 16-cycle timeout). pcpi_ready is pulsed for one cycle, and the unit waits for !pcpi_valid (S_WAIT) before accepting another instruction.
